objective: Cheapest falsification test for dir:text_to_pit_feature_extraction (registry: reports/research/harvest/directions.jsonl, status=triaged, verdict='Testable today as a small (400-sample) pilot once routed through DeepSeek instead of Claude'): DeepSeek extracts a single structured risk_score feature from 8-K filing text (10-K text is not locally available, see remaining_evidence_gap for the resulting scope narrowing from the plan's '10-K/8-K'), for a fixed-seed 50-ticker x 8-quarter (2024Q3..2026Q2) panel (400 filing-quarters), added as one feature; compute its standalone daily cross-sectional rank IC against forward 20-trading-day returns, and its IC lift over the existing factor zoo if that integration is quick, plus a mismatched-filings-across-tickers-within-quarter placebo, before any larger scale-up.
target_regime_and_horizon: 8 complete recent quarters, 2024-07-01..2026-06-30 (2024Q3 through 2026Q2), the most recent 8 fully computable quarters given forward-return needs into ~July 2026 and local data through September 2026. Universe: a fixed-seed random.Random(20260928).sample of 50 tickers from the 1146 tickers with a fetchable 8-K in ALL 8 of these quarters (data/features/earnings_events), giving exactly 400 filing-quarters. Horizon: next 20 trading days (per the brief). This pilot makes no near-term-profitability claim -- it is a go/no-go check on whether the feature (and its lift over the zoo) is real before any larger run.
existing_solution_comparison: Not invented here: Dolphin et al. (arxiv 2601.15247) show a 3-stage LLM pipeline extracts 10-K risk factors that carry real economic structure (63% higher within-industry similarity, Cohen's d=1.06); Choi et al. (arxiv 2510.03195, an 11-author LinqAlpha/MIT/BlackRock/Blackstone/JPM/Fidelity/Qube/State Street/UT-Austin/U-Florida/UNIST collaboration) show an LLM-structured disclosure-change feature beats an NER baseline by >2x risk-adjusted alpha in portfolio and cross-sectional tests; Campbell et al. (2014) independently establish that the raw (non-LLM) 10-K risk-factor section already carries real information content. This iteration's only new work is: (1) a single DeepSeek prompt returning a structured risk_score (much simpler than Dolphin et al.'s 3-stage taxonomy pipeline -- a deliberate, disclosed simplification for a cheap pilot, not a claim of matching their construction), (2) the 400 filing-quarter panel build with a PIT join, and (3) the IC + zoo-lift + placebo computation. Every input (8-K text, DeepSeek endpoint, the existing factor zoo/ranking pipeline) is already local; no new data acquisition.
remaining_evidence_gap: (1) Scope narrowing: the plan named '10-K risk classification' and '10-K/8-K'; this project's local text inventory is 8-K EX-99.1 press releases only (confirmed by dir:earnings_call_transcript_trained_embeddings_2026's own note: '335MB, 1,396 companies... 8-K press-release exhibits (EX-99.1), not verbatim call transcripts'), not 10-K Item 1A risk-factor sections. This pilot therefore extracts a risk_score from 8-K text, not 10-K text -- a real, disclosed scope change, not a silent substitution; a 10-K-text version is possible future work if this pilot shows lift. (2) Dolphin et al.'s validation is against INDUSTRY STRUCTURE, not forward RETURNS -- it does not itself establish predictive IC, which is exactly what this pilot tests. (3) Choi et al.'s evidence is on earnings-CALL transcripts (a different document type we do not have locally), not 10-K/8-K text -- supporting evidence for the general premise (LLM-structured disclosure features can beat a baseline), not a direct replication target. (4) Whether integrating the new feature into the EXISTING ranking pipeline is 'quick' is not yet known -- the brief allows reporting the standalone IC only if it is not; this iteration attempts the integration and discloses honestly which outcome occurred.
negative_experiments_checked: dir:earnings_8k_tone_next_day (refuted, h20260922_01_earnings_text/summary.json): a next-session tone-level signal on the SAME 8-K press-release text showed no next-day edge (tone vs ret_d0: ls_t=-0.77 at 10bp, ls_t=-0.77 at 20bp; the tone effect is negative-signed and not significant). This pilot differs on THREE axes at once: (a) a structured risk_score, not a tone scalar; (b) a 20-trading-day forward horizon, not next-session; (c) added as a feature into a cross-sectional ranking pipeline, not tested standalone -- distinct mechanism and horizon, not a re-run of the same test. dir:news_attention_features (refuted, L-20260916-02): count/novelty of news arrival, not filing-text risk content -- different input and mechanism entirely, does not pre-empt this direction. Checked via `oc research directions check text to pit feature extraction risk label` before starting (returned dir:text_to_pit_feature_extraction itself as status=triaged/queue-ready, not refuted, plus 8 unrelated other-status rows).
cost_and_execution_assumptions: This pilot computes only a feature, its standalone IC, and (if quick) its lift over the existing zoo; it authorizes no backtest, no cost model, and no order submission. If a later round builds a tradable signal from this feature, it reuses this project's fixed convention (close signal -> next open fill, 10bp/20bp per side), not a new one invented here. DeepSeek calls: capped by the same 5-hour rolling quota machinery reused from scripts/score_earnings_text.py (429/limit-keyword detection -> stop and checkpoint).
stop_condition: Per the brief's own rule: continue to a larger run only if the standalone (or zoo-integrated, if computed) IC lift is positive and stable-signed AND a mismatched-filings-across-tickers-within-quarter placebo does NOT reproduce it. Concretely: stop if the mean daily/quarterly rank IC does not have a stable sign (< 60% of quarters share the mean's sign), or if the placebo reproduces >=50% of the real IC's magnitude with the same sign. The risk_score prompt wording, the 50-ticker/8-quarter universe, and the 20-day horizon are fixed before any DeepSeek score is computed (see candidate-manifest.json) -- not re-picked after seeing a result.

sources.claim: A three-stage pipeline (LLM extraction with supporting quotes, embedding-based semantic mapping to a taxonomy, and LLM-as-a-judge validation) extracts 10,688 structured risk factors from S&P 500 10-K filings; external validation shows same-industry companies exhibit 63% higher risk profile similarity than cross-industry pairs (Cohen's d=1.06, AUC 0.82, p<0.001), confirming the taxonomy captures economically meaningful structure.
sources.market_and_period: S&P 500 companies, 10-K filings; 10,688 extracted risk factors; industry-cluster comparison, no specific trading-return sample.
sources.applicability: Direct methodological precedent for T-17's construction: a three-stage LLM pipeline (extraction with supporting quotes, embedding-based taxonomy mapping, LLM-as-judge validation) that turns unstructured 10-K risk-factor text into structured, taxonomy-aligned labels, and independently confirms those labels carry real economic structure (same-industry firms 63% more similar than cross-industry, Cohen's d=1.06, AUC 0.82). T-17 uses a single-DeepSeek-call simplification of this (no taxonomy mapping/judge stage), a scoped-down version, not the full pipeline.
sources.limitations: Validates that the extracted risk labels correlate with industry structure, not that they predict FORWARD RETURNS -- this paper does not itself run a trading/IC test, so it supports the feature's construction validity, not its predictive power (that is exactly what T-17's own IC pilot checks). Abstract/landing page read only, not the full paper PDF, this pass.
sources.independent_replication: Original paper (5 authors); not independently replicated by a third party this pass.

sources.claim: A framework ('LLM as extractor, embedding as ruler') extracts context-aware metric-focused spans from corporate disclosures and quantifies semantic change across consecutive periods via embedding similarity; in portfolio and cross-sectional regression tests against a recent NER-based baseline, this LLM-based method achieves more than twice the risk-adjusted alpha and shows significantly stronger predictive power.
sources.market_and_period: Corporate disclosures (earnings calls), cross-sectional regression + portfolio tests; multi-institution author list (LinqAlpha, MIT, BlackRock, Blackstone, JPMorgan, Fidelity, Qube, State Street, UT Austin, U. Florida, UNIST).
sources.applicability: The closest direct evidence for T-17's core question -- does an LLM-extracted structured semantic feature from corporate disclosures ADD predictive power (not just descriptive structure) beyond a simpler baseline: this paper's 'LLM as extractor, embedding as ruler' method achieves more than 2x the risk-adjusted alpha of an NER-based baseline and stronger cross-sectional-regression predictive power -- i.e. an LLM-structured text feature CAN beat a simpler baseline in a comparable setting, supporting the direction's premise that this is worth a cheap pilot rather than dismissing it outright.
sources.limitations: Uses earnings-CALL transcripts (metric-tracking across consecutive periods), not 10-K risk factors or 8-K press releases -- a different document type and a different LLM extraction task (metric shift, not risk-label classification) than T-17's actual construction; cited as supporting evidence that LLM-structured disclosure features can add alpha over a baseline, not as a direct replication target. Also, we do not have call-transcript data locally (see negative_experiments_checked) -- this pilot only uses 8-K text.
sources.independent_replication: Original paper; 11-author, multi-institution industry+academia collaboration, not itself a third-party replication of a prior result.

sources.claim: Beginning in 2005 the SEC mandated a 10-K 'risk factor' section; firms facing greater risk disclose more risk factors and allocate disclosure toward the risk types they actually face, and the information conveyed by risk-factor disclosures is reflected in systematic risk, idiosyncratic risk, information asymmetry, and firm value.
sources.market_and_period: US public companies, Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors, post-2005 SEC-mandated disclosure regime.
sources.applicability: Establishes the baseline finding this pilot's feature tries to sharpen with an LLM: the raw Item 1A risk-factor SECTION already carries real information (correlates with systematic risk, idiosyncratic risk, information asymmetry, and firm value) even without any LLM processing -- i.e. risk-factor text is a legitimate, previously-validated PIT information source, not a speculative one; T-17 asks whether an LLM-structured label adds INCREMENTAL cross-sectional return information beyond this known baseline content.
sources.limitations: This is about the 10-K annual Item 1A risk-factor section specifically; T-17's actual local data is 8-K quarterly press releases (EX-99.1), not 10-K Item 1A text -- a different document (see negative_experiments_checked/remaining_evidence_gap for the resulting scope narrowing). Abstract only read (repec.org listing), not the full published article.
sources.independent_replication: Original paper (Review of Accounting Studies 2014); widely cited in accounting/finance literature, not independently re-verified this pass.

sources.claim: The Loughran-McDonald Master Dictionary with sentiment word lists (most recent update March 2026, covering 1993-2025) is maintained by the University of Notre Dame's Software Repository for Accounting and Finance and is free for use in academic research.
sources.market_and_period: N/A -- word-list/dictionary resource, most recent update March 2026, covering filings 1993-2025.
sources.applicability: Documents the established, most widely used non-LLM baseline for financial-text tone scoring (Loughran-McDonald word lists), the natural comparison point T-17's DeepSeek risk-label feature should eventually be checked against if it clears this pilot's bar -- consistent with this project's rule to compare any new text feature to a simple baseline on the same data/costs, not just report it in isolation.
sources.limitations: This is the resource's own official landing page (word-list download + licensing terms), not the original 2011 Journal of Finance paper's full text -- used here to confirm the dictionary is a real, current, freely available academic resource, not to re-derive its original empirical results.
sources.independent_replication: Official maintainer page (Notre Dame SRAF); the underlying 2011 paper is one of the most widely cited and replicated in financial textual analysis.

sources.claim: Purging and embargoing (Lopez de Prado's terminology) both involve removing some of the data points near the boundaries of affected cross-validation folds in financial time series to prevent training/test label overlap.
sources.applicability: T-17's mismatched-filing-across-tickers-within-quarter placebo is this pilot's own leakage-avoidance analog to purging/embargoing: both exist to test whether an apparent predictive signal survives a deliberate break of the true label-to-feature correspondence. This source documents the standard concept; T-17 does not build a full purge/embargo CV harness, only the cheaper placebo check, consistent with this being a pilot.
sources.limitations: Third-party (QuantInsti) blog explainer of Lopez de Prado's method, not the primary book text (not freely accessible, not quoted here).
sources.independent_replication: Third-party educational provider; underlying method has multiple independent open-source implementations, not individually re-verified this pass.

sources.claim: Presents explicit formulas for 101 real-life quantitative trading alphas built from cross-sectional rank, time-series, and decay operators; average holding period 0.6-6.4 days; average pairwise alpha correlation 15.9%.
sources.market_and_period: US equities, WorldQuant proprietary alpha universe.
sources.applicability: Source of the cross-sectional-rank IC evaluation grammar reused for T-17's own rank-IC computation (same operator convention as T-16's pilot, for consistency across this round's two pilots).
sources.limitations: Contains no LLM, news, or filing-text signal; cited only for the rank/IC evaluation convention.
sources.independent_replication: Widely reused operator library in the public quant-finance literature; not independently re-verified line-by-line this pass.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Score all fetchable 8-K text for the preregistered 50-ticker x 8-quarter panel via DeepSeek, extracting risk_score in [0,1] (higher = more risk/uncertainty disclosed) plus risk_direction (up/same/down vs the filer's own prior tone, best-effort); build one feature value per (ticker, filing quarter) using each item's visible_at for the PIT join; compute cross-sectional rank IC against forward 20-trading-day return from each quarter's 8-K filing date; attempt to add risk_score as one input to the existing factor-zoo ranking pipeline and report the IC lift if that integration is quick; run the mismatched-filings-across-tickers-within-quarter placebo on the identical pipeline.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: Mean IC (standalone, and zoo-lift if computed) has a stable sign (>=60% of quarters/observations share the mean's sign) AND the placebo's mean |IC| is <50% of the real mean |IC| with the same sign.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: IC sign is not stable, or the placebo reproduces >=50% of the real IC's magnitude with the same sign -- in either case the direction is marked continue=false for this construction and not scaled beyond this 400-filing-quarter pilot.
